draft.title: Topic sentences
card: A topic sentence is the first sentence of a body paragraph. It tells the reader what the paragraph will prove.
It states one step of the argument, so each paragraph has one main point. A paragraph that tries to prove two points becomes hard to follow.
It links back to the thesis and the question, often by repeating their main ideas in new words. This shows the paragraph is answering the question.
A topic sentence makes a claim about the text. It does not just name a topic or retell the plot, and the evidence and analysis come after it.
draft.remember: Open each body paragraph with one claim that moves the thesis forward.

a.q: Which sentence is the best topic sentence for a body paragraph?
opts: The composer shows that loneliness drives the narrator's choices
This paragraph will talk about the narrator and some events
The narrator walks home alone after the party in the city
Many readers feel that loneliness is a sad thing in life
a.why: The first option makes one clear claim about the text that can be argued and proved. The third option only retells an event, so it names what happens but does not make a point about it.
a.clue: Look for one claim about the text, not a topic or a plot event.

b.q: Mia's thesis says a novel shows that hope can survive hardship. Her question is about how the composer presents hope. Which topic sentence best suits her first body paragraph?
opts: The composer presents hope as strong by having the hero keep planning
The hero loses his home early and must move to a new town
The composer uses many techniques, and the hero feels hope and fear
Hardship is a common experience for people in many places
b.why: The first option makes one claim, uses the ideas of hope and hardship from the thesis, and answers how the composer presents hope. The third option sounds relevant, but it names many ideas at once instead of one step of the argument.
b.clue: Pick the sentence with one claim that links to both the thesis and the question.
